newsitem.title: USA: Developer weighs site on Coney Island, N.Y.--paper.
newsitem.headline: Developer weighs site on Coney Island, N.Y.--paper.

text.p: A real estate developer is weighing whether to build a $100 million recreational and commercial project next to the proposed Sportsplex development on Coney Island, the Daily News reported Tuesday.

Forest City/Ratner declined comment when the paper asked it about the plan. However, the News quoted Assemblyman Clarence Norman, D-Crown Heights, who said "Bruce Ratner has indicated tremendous interest in the whole Sportsplex development."
Sportsplex is planned as a $70 million, 12,000-seat facility that would be used for local high school, college and amateur sports, as well as concerts and other indoor events.
Norman told the paper Ratner's plans include a virtual-reality amusement park complex and numerous high-tech, state-of-the-art arcades.

TAMS Consultants, hired by the Brooklyn Sports Commission, said in a report that Sportsplex and the private development would generate annual tax revenues in excess of the annual cost of paying for Sportsplex.

Adding privately funded project to Sportsplex might make a state investment in the project more attractive to New York State Gov George Pataki and the Empire State Development Corp, the paper said. Initial state funding for Sportsplex has yet to be approved.
